title: Checkpoint and resolved progress can diverge during sink retry
source_heading_path: TiCDC progress, sink retry, and recovery boundary > Checkpoint and resolved progress
use_when: Use when a replication endpoint looks healthy but checkpoint, resolved, and source progress do not agree.
follow_up: Compare the same time window in the raw sink log and changefeed status before selecting a recovery boundary.
content: Checkpoint reports the latest change event successfully applied by the sink; resolved reports a source frontier, so resolved can move past a sink-retry event while checkpoint remains blocked.

title: A normal control-plane state is not sink catch-up proof
source_heading_path: TiCDC progress, sink retry, and recovery boundary > Checkpoint and resolved progress
use_when: Use when REST state is normal but business freshness is behind.
follow_up: Do not stop at the state field; correlate checkpoint, resolved, source TSO, and the retry error.
content: A healthy-looking changefeed control-plane state does not prove sink catch-up; compare state, checkpoint, resolved, source progress, and raw sink logs in one time window.

title: Resume after the isolated failed DDL event
source_heading_path: TiCDC progress, sink retry, and recovery boundary > Recovery boundary
use_when: Use after isolating one sink DDL failure and repairing the downstream schema.
follow_up: Verify replay with checkpoint, resolved progress, source progress, and business-row equality.
content: Use the unique failed DDL event commit timestamp from raw TiCDC retry logs, then resume the same feed from the first timestamp after that event; do not use a later current TSO.

title: Timestamp defaults depend on session time semantics
source_heading_path: Timestamp DDL and session time semantics > Timestamp defaults are session-sensitive
use_when: Use when the same temporal DDL succeeds upstream and fails in a MySQL-compatible downstream session.
follow_up: Compare the DDL text with upstream and downstream session/global time-zone values.
content: A TIMESTAMP default is interpreted with session time semantics, so an upstream lower-bound literal can be rejected by a downstream session with a different timezone.

title: Equivalent timestamp DDL can use a different display value
source_heading_path: Timestamp DDL and session time semantics > Cross-endpoint diagnosis
use_when: Use when validating a downstream schema repair across different endpoint time zones.
follow_up: Validate type, nullability, and default semantics before resuming the feed.
content: Equivalent downstream timestamp DDL may display the same UTC instant with a local clock value; validate type, nullability, and default through SHOW CREATE TABLE and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

title: Table-bound slow work is an independent sink bottleneck
source_heading_path: Sink backpressure, healthy neighbors, and closed-loop validation > Independent sink capacity
use_when: Use when replication lag persists after a DDL blocker is bypassed or when only one downstream table is slow.
follow_up: Inspect table, event, body, and latency for all hooks; compare a healthy neighboring path.
content: Table-bound slow write hooks reduce sink capacity independently of cluster health; identify them by table, event, body, and latency, and preserve healthy neighboring paths.

title: Replication recovery requires a multi-source closed loop
source_heading_path: Sink backpressure, healthy neighbors, and closed-loop validation > Acceptance and safety
use_when: Use for final acceptance after a changefeed DDL retry and sink-capacity repair.
follow_up: Check every invariant independently; a successful control-plane command is not final recovery evidence.
content: Closed-loop recovery requires changefeed progress, equivalent DDL, complete source and downstream business rows including post-event writes, sink capacity, healthy neighbors, and core service health.
